experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution to witness the aurora borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind the lights while waiting for nature's greatest show.
experiences.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir area, Southwest Iceland

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, a silica mud mask bar, and a swim-up bar serving Icelandic craft beer. Booking the evening slot dramatically increases your chances of seeing the northern lights from the warm water.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool dating back to 1891 surrounded by geysers and hot springs. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic local experience offers a peaceful soak with stunning rural scenery and occasional northern lights overhead.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore the colorful streets of downtown Reykjavik with a local guide, sampling traditional Icelandic dishes including skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), fermented shark (hákarl), and fresh langoustine. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church, the Harpa Concert Hall, and local art galleries to absorb Iceland's unique Viking-rooted culture.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's stunning rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands and reward yourself with a natural geothermal hot spring soak at the end of the trail. The vivid green, red, and yellow volcanic landscape is unlike anywhere on Earth, and the natural pool is the perfect way to soothe tired muscles under open skies.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the budget-friendly Flybus shuttle (approx. 3,500 ISK) from the airport to Reykjavik, then connect to your hotel transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront accommodation. If skies are clear, step outside briefly to scan for the Northern Lights from the hotel grounds.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In flight
meals.lunch: N/A - In flight
meals.dinner: Grab a quick budget snack at Keflavik Airport (sandwiches or soup from airport cafeteria, approx. 1,500-2,000 ISK) or pick up instant noodles/snacks from a convenience store near the hotel upon arrival.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange a small amount of currency or ensure your card works for contactless payments. Download the Vedur app (Icelandic Met Office) for real-time Northern Lights forecasts. January temperatures average -1°C to 3°C — dress in warm layers immediately upon landing.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from jet lag. Enjoy a slow morning at the hotel. Walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to take in the dramatic Icelandic coastal scenery. Sunrise is around 11:00 AM in January, so don't rush — enjoy the moody pre-dawn light over the ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into Reykjavik city center (bus or rideshare, approx. 500-800 ISK). Explore the iconic Hallgrimskirkja Church (exterior free, tower entry ~1,000 ISK). Walk along Laugavegur Street, browse local shops and street art. Visit the Harpa Concert Hall exterior and waterfront boardwalk — completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel area before dark (around 16:30). After dinner, bundle up and head to a dark spot near the hotel beach or a nearby hill for your first serious Northern Lights watch. Check the Vedur app for KP index — January offers some of the best aurora chances of the year.

meals.breakfast: Cook instant oatmeal or grab bread and spreads from a nearby Bonus supermarket (budget staple). Stock up on groceries today — Bonus is Iceland's cheapest supermarket chain.
meals.lunch: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur hot dog stand in Reykjavik — famous Icelandic hot dogs for ~500 ISK each. A true budget traveler's must.
meals.dinner: Self-catered meal at the hotel using groceries from Bonus. Pasta with sauce, eggs, or soup — budget approx. 800-1,200 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: January daylight is extremely limited (roughly 5-6 hours). Plan outdoor sightseeing between 10:30 AM and 4:00 PM. Pick up a 10-ride Strætó bus card for cheaper city transport. Northern Lights viewing is best between 21:00-02:00 on clear nights.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the famous Reykjanes Peninsula geothermal area — accessible by bus or a shared day tour (budget tours from ~3,000-5,000 ISK). Explore the Bridge Between Continents (free), a symbolic footbridge spanning the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates. Walk the dramatic lava fields nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Gunnuhver Hot Springs and mud pools on the Reykjanes Peninsula — entry is free. See the powerful geothermal steam vents up close. Walk the marked trails around the area. Stop at the Reykjanes Lighthouse for sweeping coastal views — free and stunning.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel. Tonight, prioritize a Northern Lights hunt. Drive or walk to a dark coastal area near the hotel. The beachfront location is excellent for unobstructed northern horizon views. Bring a thermos of hot tea or cocoa, a blanket, and your camera/tripod if available.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel — bread, eggs, yogurt from Bonus supermarket (approx. 400-600 ISK).
meals.lunch: Pack a homemade lunch — sandwiches, fruit, and snacks from Bonus to eat at the geothermal area. Saves significantly vs. restaurant costs.
meals.dinner: Noodles, canned soup, or a simple stir-fry at the hotel. Budget 800-1,000 ISK. Alternatively, try Aktu Taktu fast food chain in Reykjavik for a budget burger meal (~1,500 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy waterproof boots — geothermal areas can have muddy, uneven terrain. The Reykjanes area is about 20-30 minutes from Keflavik/Reykjavik. Some budget tour operators offer combo Reykjanes + Northern Lights tours for around 7,000-9,000 ISK — worth considering.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget Golden Circle day tour (from ~8,000-12,000 ISK including transport) or rent a car with fellow travelers to split costs. First stop: Þingvellir (Thingvellir) National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where you can walk the rift valley between tectonic plates. Entry to the park is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area — watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5-10 minutes. Entry is free. Then visit Gullfoss Waterfall — one of Iceland's most powerful waterfalls. Completely free to visit. The winter views with potential ice formations are spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Return from the Golden Circle (back by 18:00-19:00). Rest briefly, then head out for Northern Lights viewing. The Golden Circle area, especially Þingvellir, has very low light pollution — if the tour ends late enough, ask the driver to stop for aurora viewing.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered hotel breakfast — oatmeal, fruit, coffee (400-600 ISK).
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks for the Golden Circle. Restaurants at Geysir area are expensive (~3,000-4,000 ISK for a meal). Saving here is crucial for budget travelers.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at hotel. Treat yourself slightly — try making a simple Icelandic skyr bowl with granola and berries (skyr is cheap and nutritious, ~300-400 ISK at Bonus).

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle is approximately 300 km round trip. If renting a car, ensure it has 4WD for January winter conditions. Roads can be icy — check road.is for conditions before departing. Dress in your warmest layers — wind chill at Gullfoss in January can be severe.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Reykjavik Old Harbour area. Visit the free Grandi Mathöll food hall for a browse (budget a small treat ~800-1,200 ISK). Walk to the Sun Voyager sculpture (Sólfar) on the waterfront — free and iconic, especially beautiful in winter light. Visit the Faxaflói Bay viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) — entry fee ~2,000 ISK, but offers deep insight into Icelandic history and culture. Alternatively, the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) is ~2,200 ISK and showcases a real Viking-age longhouse discovered under the city. Choose one to stay on budget.
day_by_day.evening: Free Northern Lights hunt evening. Check aurora forecast — if KP index is 3 or above and skies are clear, head to Öskjuhlíð Hill (Perlan area) in Reykjavik for a great dark sky spot within the city. The Perlan Northern Lights exhibit is paid, but the hilltop itself is free to access.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel (400-600 ISK).
meals.lunch: Hlöllabátar submarine sandwich shop in Reykjavik — affordable and filling sandwiches for ~1,200-1,500 ISK. A local budget favorite.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at hotel. Try a hearty lentil or vegetable soup — cheap, warming, and nutritious for cold January evenings. Budget 600-900 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: January 19 has approximately 5.5 hours of daylight. Plan museum visits to maximize the limited afternoon light and save outdoor activities for the brief midday window. Reykjavik's compact city center is very walkable — saves on transport costs.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the South Coast. Take a budget tour or rent a car. First stop: Seljalandsfoss Waterfall — you can walk behind this stunning 60-meter waterfall (entry free, parking fee ~750 ISK). In winter, the ice formations make it magical. Nearby Gljúfrabúi hidden waterfall is also free and less crowded.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Skógafoss Waterfall — another massive, free-to-visit waterfall with a staircase to the top for panoramic views. Then drive to Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach near Vík — one of the world's most dramatic beaches with basalt column formations and sea stacks. Completely free, but respect ocean warning signs (sneaker waves are dangerous).
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return journey toward the hotel. If driving, stop at a dark roadside pullout on the way back for Northern Lights viewing — the South Coast has minimal light pollution. Return to hotel by 21:00-22:00.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel before early departure (aim to leave by 08:30-09:00).
meals.lunch: Pack a substantial packed lunch — this is a long day trip. Sandwiches, energy bars, fruit, and a thermos of hot soup or coffee.
meals.dinner: If passing through Vík, try Ströndin Bistro for a budget meal (~2,000-2,500 ISK) or grab a hot dog from a gas station (N1 or Orkan stations — hot dogs are ~400-600 ISK and surprisingly good). Self-cater at hotel if returning late.

day_by_day.notes: South Coast day trips are approximately 250-300 km round trip from Reykjavik. Check road.is — Route 1 (Ring Road) is generally well-maintained but can have ice patches in January. Waterfalls may be partially frozen, adding to their winter beauty. Wear microspike ice cleats if available.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day and mid-trip recovery. Sleep in and have a leisurely morning at the hotel. Walk the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort, enjoy the winter seascape, and take photos of the dramatic Icelandic coastal landscape. Do laundry if needed — many hostels and hotels have coin-operated machines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local public swimming pool (sundlaug) — Iceland's public pools are incredibly affordable (approx. 1,000-1,200 ISK) and are geothermally heated. They include hot tubs (heitir pottar) at various temperatures. This is authentic Icelandic culture and a great way to warm up. The Reykjanes area has several local pools.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed Northern Lights evening. Prepare a warm dinner at the hotel, check the aurora forecast carefully, and position yourself at the best dark spot near the hotel. January 21 is mid-winter — statistically excellent aurora conditions if skies cooperate.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer self-catered breakfast — Icelandic skyr with honey, rye bread (rúgbrauð) with butter, and fresh coffee (700-900 ISK total).
meals.lunch: Self-catered lunch at hotel — leftover soup, sandwiches, or eggs (400-600 ISK).
meals.dinner: Cook a proper meal at the hotel — try making a simple lamb or fish stew using affordable cuts from Bonus supermarket. Lamb is relatively affordable in Iceland (~1,200-1,500 ISK for ingredients for two).

day_by_day.notes: Public swimming pools are a quintessential Icelandic experience — don't miss it! Follow pool etiquette: shower thoroughly without swimsuit before entering. Bring your own towel to avoid rental fees. This is also a great day to plan the second half of your trip and check weather forecasts.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Snæfellsnes Peninsula (long day trip — depart by 07:30-08:00). Drive or join a budget tour. First stop: Kirkjufell Mountain — Iceland's most photographed mountain, especially stunning in winter. Free to view and photograph. The nearby Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall is equally beautiful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along Snæfellsnes to Snæfellsjökull National Park. Visit Djúpalónssandur Black Pebble Beach (free) with dramatic rock formations and rusty shipwreck remains. Drive to Arnarstapi village for stunning coastal basalt cliff formations and arch rock — all free. The glacier Snæfellsjökull (of Jules Verne fame) looms above.
day_by_day.evening: Begin return journey (approximately 2.5-3 hours back to Reykjavik area). If aurora forecast is good, stop at a dark roadside area on the Snæfellsnes Peninsula before heading back — this remote area has exceptional dark skies. Return to hotel by 22:00-23:00.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before departure — energy-dense foods like oatmeal, peanut butter on toast, bananas (500-700 ISK).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Kirkjufell or Djúpalónssandur beach — sandwiches, thermos of soup, snacks.
meals.dinner: Stop at a gas station in Borgarnes on the return for a hot dog and coffee (~600-800 ISK) or self-cater at hotel upon return.

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is approximately 180 km from Reykjavik — a full day is needed. Budget tours to Snæfellsnes run ~10,000-15,000 ISK. Car rental split between 2-4 people is often cheaper. Road conditions on the peninsula can be challenging in January — 4WD strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Reykjavik flea market, Kolaportið (open weekends, 11:00-17:00) — browse vintage Icelandic clothing, local food items like hákarl (fermented shark) and dried fish, and handmade crafts. Entry is free and it's a fascinating cultural experience. Pick up budget souvenirs here rather than tourist shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a bus to Öskjuhlíð Hill and the Perlan building. The exterior viewing deck offers 360° panoramic views of Reykjavik and surrounding mountains — free to access the grounds. Explore the geothermal hot water storage tanks. Walk through the surrounding nature trails (free). Visit Nauthólsvík Geothermal Beach nearby — a unique artificially warmed beach (free in winter).
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights hunt from Öskjuhlíð Hill or return to hotel's beachfront. This is a statistically good aurora window — mid-January through February has long, dark nights. Set an alarm for 22:00 and 01:00 to check conditions throughout the night.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel (400-600 ISK).
meals.lunch: Try Icelandic-style open-faced sandwiches (smørrebrød-style) from a bakery like Sandholt Bakery in Reykjavik (~1,200-1,500 ISK). A slight splurge but worth it for quality local food.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at hotel — pasta with a simple cream and smoked salmon sauce (smoked salmon is surprisingly affordable at Bonus, ~800-1,000 ISK for ingredients).

day_by_day.notes: Kolaportið flea market is only open Saturday and Sunday — check that January 23 falls on a weekend in 2027 (it's a Saturday ✓). This is a great day for cultural immersion without major expenses. Keep a running tally of your budget to ensure you're on track for the final days.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Krýsuvík Geothermal Area on the Reykjanes Peninsula — colorful hot springs, bubbling mud pools, and steaming fumaroles set in a dramatic volcanic landscape. Entry is completely free. Walk the marked boardwalk trails around the geothermal field. The vivid yellow sulfur deposits and turquoise pools are otherworldly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or bus to Lake Kleifarvatn nearby — Iceland's largest lake on the Reykjanes Peninsula, set in a stark lava landscape. Free to visit. Walk along the lake shore for dramatic winter scenery. Continue to Seltún geothermal area (part of Krýsuvík system) for more colorful hot spring formations — free.
day_by_day.evening: Return to hotel area. Treat yourself to a budget soak — many geothermal pools in the Reykjanes area are free or very low cost. Alternatively, visit a local public pool for a relaxing evening soak in the hot tubs. Northern Lights check before bed.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel (400-600 ISK).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Krýsuvík — the area has no restaurants, so packing food is essential. Hot soup in a thermos is ideal for cold January conditions.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at hotel. Try making Icelandic lamb soup (kjötsúpa) — lamb neck pieces from Bonus are inexpensive (~800 ISK), add root vegetables and barley for a hearty, authentic Icelandic meal (~1,000-1,200 ISK total).

day_by_day.notes: Krýsuvík is approximately 40 km from Reykjavik. The geothermal area boardwalks can be icy in January — wear ice cleats or boots with good grip. Do not step off marked paths near hot springs — ground can be dangerously thin over boiling water. This area has extremely low light pollution for Northern Lights viewing.

day_by_day.morning: Final major day trip: explore the area around Hveragerði — Iceland's geothermal greenhouse town, about 45 minutes from Reykjavik. Walk the famous Reykjadalur Hot River Trail (free) — a 3 km hike each way leading to a natural geothermal river where you can bathe. In January, the hike is snowy and magical.
day_by_day.afternoon: Soak in the Reykjadalur hot river (bring swimsuit and towel — changing facilities are basic). The contrast of soaking in warm geothermal water surrounded by snow-covered hills is an unforgettable Icelandic experience. Return hike to Hveragerði. Browse the town's geothermal greenhouses and bakeries briefly.
day_by_day.evening: Return to hotel. This is your second-to-last full day — do a Northern Lights vigil if conditions are favorable. January 25 still has excellent aurora potential. Pack non-essential items to begin preparing for departure.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before hiking departure — energy-rich foods (oatmeal, nuts, banana) — 500-700 ISK.
meals.lunch: Pack lunch for the trail — you'll be hiking and soaking, so bring sandwiches, energy bars, and a large thermos of hot tea or cocoa. No food available on the trail.
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner on this near-last night. Try Hveragerði's local bakery for fresh bread and soup (~1,500 ISK) or splurge modestly at a Reykjavik budget restaurant like Hlemmur Mathöll food hall (~2,000-2,500 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjadalur hike is rated moderate but can be challenging in January with snow and ice. Microspike crampons are strongly recommended. The hot river temperature varies — test before fully immersing. Bring a dry bag for your clothes while soaking. Allow 3-4 hours total for the round trip hike and soaking time.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day in Iceland. Return to any favorite spots or fill in missed activities. Consider a final walk along the Reykjavik waterfront and Old Harbour area. Visit the Árbær Open Air Museum (approx. 1,800 ISK) if not yet visited — a collection of historic Icelandic turf houses and buildings. Check opening hours in January.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at Kolaportið flea market (if open) or Bonus supermarket for affordable Icelandic gifts: skyr, dried fish, licorice, Icelandic sea salt, and locally made jams. These are far cheaper than tourist shop equivalents. Pack bags and prepare for tomorrow's departure.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights attempt — this is your last chance! Head to the darkest accessible spot near the hotel. If the aurora forecast is favorable (KP 3+, clear skies), this could be the highlight of your trip. Stay out until midnight if conditions are good. Celebrate your Iceland trip with a hot cocoa under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel — use up remaining groceries (400-600 ISK).
meals.lunch: Final Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur hot dog pilgrimage in Reykjavik — a perfect budget farewell meal (~500-600 ISK).
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner — slightly splurge at Reykjavik Fish Restaurant or try Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) for famous lobster soup (~1,500 ISK per bowl) — a beloved Reykjavik institution that's relatively affordable by Icelandic standards.

day_by_day.notes: Use up any remaining Icelandic króna on food and small gifts — currency exchange at the airport gives poor rates. Ensure all laundry is done and bags are packed tonight. Set multiple alarms for tomorrow's departure. Review your budget for the trip and celebrate your savings — Iceland on a budget is an achievement!

day_by_day.morning: Departure day. Wake up early, enjoy a final self-catered breakfast using remaining hotel food supplies. Do a final room check — ensure nothing is left behind. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Take the Flybus or arrange transport to Keflavik International Airport (approx. 3,500 ISK for Flybus). Arrive at airport at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Airport time — check in, clear security, and browse duty-free for any last Icelandic items (Brennivín schnapps, Icelandic chocolates, or cosmetics are popular duty-free picks). Reflect on 13 incredible days in Iceland.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Board your return flight with memories of the Northern Lights, geothermal hot springs, dramatic waterfalls, black sand beaches, and the raw, volcanic beauty of Iceland.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered final breakfast at hotel using remaining groceries — keep it simple and use everything up.
meals.lunch: Airport meal — budget for one airport meal (~2,000-2,500 ISK). Keflavik Airport has a Dunkin' Donuts and several cafes that are more affordable than sit-down restaurants.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport meal depending on flight time.

day_by_day.notes: Budget Summary Estimate for 13 days per person: Accommodation (Aegean Bliss Resort - 12 nights): Variable. Food (mostly self-catered): ~15,000-20,000 ISK. Transport (Flybus x2, buses, shared tours): ~25,000-35,000 ISK. Activities and entrance fees: ~15,000-20,000 ISK. Miscellaneous/souvenirs: ~5,000-10,000 ISK. Total estimated daily spend (excluding accommodation): ~5,000-7,000 ISK (~$35-50 USD) per day. Iceland on a budget is challenging but absolutely achievable with smart self-catering, free natural attractions, and shared transportation costs.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives late evening
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled. Grab a light snack from the hotel's lobby bar or vending area if available.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at departure airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at departure airport
meals.dinner: Light snack at hotel upon arrival — grab something from the hotel bar or a convenience store near the airport en route

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is purely arrival and rest. January nights in Iceland are long and extremely cold (average -1°C to 4°C). Pack warm layers in your carry-on for immediate use upon landing. The drive from Keflavik to most resort areas takes 45–60 minutes. Rest well — big days ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. Enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort. Take a slow morning walk along the beachfront to breathe in the crisp Icelandic sea air and get your first real look at the dramatic coastal landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa (pre-book in advance — this is essential). Soak in the iconic milky-blue geothermal waters, enjoy an in-water silica mud mask, and relax in the mineral-rich thermal pools. The Blue Lagoon is approximately 20–30 minutes from the Reykjanes Peninsula area — perfect for a first full day.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort, freshen up, and head into the nearest town for a welcome dinner. Explore a cozy Icelandic restaurant for a proper first meal in the country.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy skyr, smoked salmon, rye bread, and Icelandic pastries
meals.lunch: Light meal or snack at the Blue Lagoon's in-water Lava Restaurant or the casual bar (mid-range option: soup and bread)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant near the resort — try Icelandic lamb soup (kjötsúpa) or pan-seared Arctic char at a mid-range bistro

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon tickets MUST be pre-booked online — walk-ins are not accepted. Comfort package (~$80–100 USD) is the best mid-range option. Bring a waterproof hair tie and avoid submerging your hair in the silica-rich water to prevent tangles. January daylight is very limited (sunrise ~11:00, sunset ~15:30).

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, join the Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour. Explore the colorful streets of downtown Reykjavik with a local guide, sampling traditional Icelandic foods including skyr, hákarl (fermented shark), lamb, and local craft beers. Visit iconic landmarks like Hallgrímskirkja Church and the Harpa Concert Hall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Reykjavik independently after the tour. Visit the Sun Voyager sculpture by the harbor, browse the Laugavegur shopping street for Icelandic wool sweaters (lopapeysa), and pop into local galleries or the Settlement Exhibition museum.
day_by_day.evening: Dine in Reykjavik before returning to the resort. Check the northern lights forecast app (Vedur.is) — if aurora activity is high (KP index 3+) and skies are clear, step outside after dinner for a spontaneous northern lights viewing from a dark spot near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Included tastings on the Food & Culture Walking Tour — supplement with a bowl of lobster bisque (humarsúpa) at Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) in Reykjavik harbor
meals.dinner: Reykjavik mid-range restaurant — try Matur og Drykkur for traditional Icelandic cuisine or Snaps Bistro for French-Icelandic fusion (budget ~$30–45 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Food & Culture Walking Tour runs approximately 3 hours. Wear very warm, waterproof boots and layered clothing — Reykjavik in January is windy and cold. Download the Vedur.is northern lights app now and set up alerts for the entire trip.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on the classic Golden Circle self-drive or guided tour. First stop: Þingvellir (Thingvellir) National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk the dramatic rift valley and learn about Iceland's ancient parliament, the Althing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area — watch the famous Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting water 20–30 meters into the air. Then visit Gullfoss Waterfall, one of Iceland's most powerful and spectacular waterfalls, partially frozen and breathtaking in January.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. This is an excellent evening for the Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep tour — book this for tonight if aurora forecast is favorable. A small-group guided jeep takes you away from light pollution into the wilderness for the best possible aurora viewing.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — fuel up for a long day
meals.lunch: Cafeteria-style lunch at Geysir Center or Gullfoss Café — lamb soup, sandwiches, and hot chocolate to warm up (~$15–20)
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant or a nearby restaurant upon return — hearty meal of pan-fried lamb or fish of the day

day_by_day.notes: The full Golden Circle loop is approximately 300 km and takes 6–8 hours including stops. January roads can be icy — if self-driving, rent a 4WD vehicle and check road conditions at road.is before departing. A guided Golden Circle tour is a stress-free mid-range alternative (~$60–80 per person).

day_by_day.morning: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — if you booked this for last night and conditions were poor, tonight is your backup. This morning, enjoy a relaxed hotel breakfast and a slow start. Use the morning to plan the week ahead, do laundry, and rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Reykjanes Peninsula's geothermal wonders close to the resort. Explore the Bridge Between Continents (a walkway spanning the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates), the Gunnuhver hot spring mud pools, and the Reykjanes Lighthouse — Iceland's oldest lighthouse. All are within 20–30 minutes of the beachfront resort area.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — join tonight's small-group guided tour into the dark Icelandic wilderness. Your expert guide will track aurora forecasts in real time and drive to optimal viewing locations. Wrap up in provided blankets and watch the sky come alive with green, purple, and white dancing lights.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from the hotel or stop at a local petrol station bakery (gas station bakeries in Iceland are surprisingly excellent — try a meat soup and a kleina pastry, ~$10)
meals.dinner: Early dinner before the evening jeep tour — warm up with Icelandic fish stew or lamb at a local restaurant near the resort (~$25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep typically departs around 20:00–21:00 and returns around midnight. Dress in your absolute warmest layers — temperatures with wind chill can feel like -15°C or colder. The tour guides cannot guarantee aurora sightings as they depend on solar activity and cloud cover, but January offers the longest dark hours of the year — your best chance!

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the late-night aurora hunt. Sleep in, have a leisurely hotel breakfast, and enjoy the beachfront resort amenities — if the resort has a hot tub or pool, this is a perfect morning to use it.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or join a guided tour to the South Coast of Iceland. Visit Seljalandsfoss Waterfall — a stunning 60-meter waterfall you can walk behind (bring waterproof gear!). Then continue to Skógafoss Waterfall, equally dramatic and often with beautiful ice formations in January.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort via the scenic coastal road. Stop at a small village restaurant or a roadside café for a warm dinner. Keep an eye on the sky during the drive back — the South Coast has minimal light pollution and is excellent for aurora spotting from the car.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — take your time
meals.lunch: Skógafoss Café near the waterfall — hot soup, sandwiches, and coffee (~$15–20)
meals.dinner: Cozy restaurant in Hvolsvöllur or Selfoss on the return route — try slow-roasted lamb shank or grilled salmon (~$30–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Seljalandsfoss path behind the waterfall may be closed or icy in January — check locally before attempting. The South Coast drive is approximately 1.5–2 hours from the Reykjanes area. Sunset is around 15:30, so plan to be at the waterfalls during midday for the best light. The golden hour light in January is magical and lasts for hours.

day_by_day.morning: Midway point — treat yourself to a relaxing morning at the hotel. Enjoy breakfast and then head to the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir. Iceland's oldest swimming pool, naturally heated to a perfect 38–40°C, surrounded by geysers and hot spring activity. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon and equally magical.
day_by_day.afternoon: After soaking at the Secret Lagoon, explore the charming village of Flúðir and the surrounding geothermal area. Visit the small local greenhouse tomato farms (unique to Iceland's geothermal energy use). Begin the scenic drive back toward the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory mid-trip dinner at the hotel restaurant or a nicer restaurant nearby. Reflect on the week's adventures over a glass of Icelandic craft beer or a local spirit. Check aurora forecast for a potential late-night viewing from the hotel's beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Light snack or soup at the Secret Lagoon's café or in Flúðir village — try fresh Icelandic tomato soup made from locally grown greenhouse tomatoes
meals.dinner: Slightly elevated mid-range dinner — hotel restaurant or a nearby spot serving Icelandic tasting plates, fresh fish, and local cheeses (~$40–55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Secret Lagoon admission is approximately $25–30 USD — much more affordable than the Blue Lagoon. Pre-booking is recommended but not always mandatory in January (lower tourist season). Flúðir is approximately 1.5 hours from the Reykjanes Peninsula. Bring your own towel or rent one on-site.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for a full-day excursion to Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon — one of Iceland's most breathtaking natural wonders. Watch enormous icebergs calve from Breiðamerkurjökull glacier and drift through the lagoon. In January, the lagoon may be partially frozen, creating a surreal crystalline landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Diamond Beach (just across the road from Jökulsárlón) where translucent ice chunks wash ashore on black volcanic sand — a photographer's dream. Explore the nearby Fjallsárlón Glacier Lagoon for a quieter, equally stunning alternative. Begin the long drive back.
day_by_day.evening: Stop for dinner in the town of Vík or Kirkjubæjarklaustur on the return journey — both have good mid-range dining options. Arrive back at the resort late evening. Check aurora forecast — the drive back along the South Coast is prime aurora territory.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or pack a to-go breakfast from the hotel for the road
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at Jökulsárlón Café near the lagoon — hot drinks, soup, and sandwiches are available seasonally (confirm winter opening hours in advance)
meals.dinner: Restaurant in Vík — try Suður-Vík restaurant for fish and chips, lamb burgers, or Icelandic seafood soup (~$25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Jökulsárlón is approximately 4.5–5 hours from the Reykjanes area — this is a very long day (300+ km each way). Consider booking a guided South Coast & Glacier Lagoon full-day tour (~$120–150 per person) to avoid driving fatigue on potentially icy roads. Alternatively, split this into two days by staying overnight near Vík. January road conditions on Route 1 can be challenging — always check road.is.

day_by_day.morning: Well-deserved rest morning after the long glacier lagoon day. Sleep in, enjoy a slow hotel breakfast, and use the hotel's amenities. If the resort has a spa, book a treatment this morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Reykjanes Peninsula's unique volcanic landscape close to the resort. Visit the Svartsengi geothermal power plant area (the source of the Blue Lagoon's waters), walk the Reykjanesviti lighthouse trail, and explore the dramatic lava fields of Eldvörp. These otherworldly landscapes are just minutes from the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Second Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep (if you haven't had a successful viewing yet, or want another chance). January offers the longest dark hours — maximum opportunity. Alternatively, enjoy a quiet evening at the resort with dinner and aurora watching from the beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — leisurely pace
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel or a nearby café — Icelandic open-faced sandwiches (smørrebrød style) with smoked salmon and cream cheese
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant dinner or local restaurant — try Icelandic beef tenderloin or catch-of-the-day fish with roasted root vegetables (~$30–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula was dramatically affected by volcanic eruptions in 2021–2024. Some areas may have new lava fields or restricted access. Check local updates for the latest access information. The peninsula's geothermal activity makes it one of the most geologically active places on Earth — a fascinating afternoon exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Snæfellsnes Peninsula — home to the iconic Snæfellsjökull glacier volcano (immortalized in Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth'). Depart early and drive north. First stop: Kirkjufell Mountain, Iceland's most photographed mountain, with the nearby Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue around the Snæfellsnes Peninsula: visit Arnarstapi coastal cliffs with dramatic basalt formations and sea arches, Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach with its mysterious lifting stones, and Snæfellsjökull National Park visitor center. The glacier-capped volcano looms dramatically over the entire peninsula.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the drive back to the resort (approximately 2.5–3 hours). Stop for dinner in Borgarnes or Akranes on the return route. Arrive back at the resort by late evening.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast — fuel up for the long drive
meals.lunch: Restaurant in Arnarstapi village or Hellnar — try fresh langoustine soup or fish of the day at a small local eatery (~$20–30)
meals.dinner: Borgarnes Settlement Center Restaurant on the return route — known for excellent Icelandic food and an interesting Viking history exhibition (~$30–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is approximately 2.5–3 hours from the Reykjanes area. This is a full-day commitment (10–12 hours total). A guided Snæfellsnes tour is available and recommended for winter driving safety. The peninsula is stunning in January with snow-capped mountains and moody winter light. Kirkjufell is particularly magical with ice and snow.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at the resort — you've earned it after the big Snæfellsnes day. Enjoy breakfast, pack any souvenirs, and do a final check of your aurora hunt wish list. If the Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike is on your agenda, today is the day to check feasibility (NOTE: Landmannalaugar is typically inaccessible in January due to deep snow and closed mountain roads — confirm with local operators).
day_by_day.afternoon: Alternative to Landmannalaugar: Visit the Krýsuvík geothermal area on the Reykjanes Peninsula — bubbling mud pools, steaming sulfuric vents, and colorful mineral deposits in a dramatic volcanic landscape. Hike the easy Seltún geothermal trail (30–45 minutes) and enjoy the raw geothermal energy up close.
day_by_day.evening: Reykjavik evening out — head into the capital for a final proper city night. Explore the Laugavegur bar and restaurant scene, visit a craft beer bar like Skúli Craft Bar or Mikkeller & Friends, and enjoy live music or local entertainment.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch near Krýsuvík or grab food at a petrol station bakery — hot soup in a thermos from the hotel is ideal for outdoor exploration
meals.dinner: Reykjavik dinner out — try Grillmarkaðurinn (The Grill Market) for premium Icelandic ingredients at mid-to-upper range pricing, or Messinn for excellent pan-fried fish at very reasonable prices (~$25–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: IMPORTANT: Landmannalaugar is almost certainly inaccessible in January due to F-road closures (mountain roads require super jeeps and are often completely snowed in). Do not attempt without professional highland guide confirmation. The Krýsuvík geothermal area is an excellent and accessible alternative that showcases Iceland's geothermal wonders.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning — sleep in and enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Take a long, reflective beachfront walk along the resort's coastline. Watch for seabirds, enjoy the dramatic winter seascape, and soak in the last views of Iceland's rugged coastal beauty.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik for last-minute souvenir shopping on Laugavegur Street. Pick up lopapeysa (Icelandic wool sweaters), local chocolates, Icelandic sea salt, skyr products, and Viking-themed gifts. Visit the Kolaportið flea market (open weekends) for unique local finds and cheap Icelandic snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Northern Lights attempt — one final evening aurora hunt. Either join a Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep tour for a last guided attempt, or drive to a dark spot near the resort for independent viewing. End the evening with a celebratory farewell dinner at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — savor it!
meals.lunch: Quick lunch in Reykjavik while shopping — Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur (the famous Reykjavik hot dog stand, a must-do Icelandic experience, ~$3–5)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the hotel restaurant or a nearby special restaurant — splurge slightly on a memorable final meal: Icelandic lamb, fresh fish, and a local dessert like skyr cake (~$40–55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur hot dogs are an Icelandic institution — order 'one with everything' (eina með öllu) for the full experience. January is low season so shopping lines are minimal. If you haven't successfully seen the northern lights yet, tonight is your penultimate chance — January KP activity can be strong and unpredictable, so stay hopeful!

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Pack, check out of Aegean Bliss Resort, and enjoy one last hotel breakfast. If time permits before airport transfer, take a quick final dip in a local geothermal pool or hot pot — many Icelanders start their day this way and it's the perfect goodbye to Iceland's hot spring culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Keflavik International Airport (45–60 minutes from most resort areas). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in, security, and duty-free shopping. Pick up last-minute Icelandic spirits (Brennivín schnapps), chocolates, or skincare products from the Blue Lagoon brand at the airport duty-free.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland with incredible memories of aurora hunts, geothermal soaks, volcanic landscapes, and Icelandic hospitality. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy every bite of that skyr and smoked salmon
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café at Keflavik — try a final bowl of Icelandic lamb soup before boarding
meals.dinner: On the plane or at your connecting airport

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at most Icelandic hotels is 11:00–12:00. Confirm your checkout time with the resort. Keflavik Airport has excellent duty-free shopping — Icelandic alcohol is significantly cheaper at the airport than in stores due to Iceland's alcohol regulations. Leave extra luggage space for woolens and souvenirs! Double-check that all rental cars are returned and that you have your passport, boarding pass, and travel documents ready.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution to witness the aurora borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind the lights while waiting for nature's greatest show.
experiences.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir area, Southwest Iceland

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, a silica mud mask bar, and a swim-up bar serving Icelandic craft beer. Booking the evening slot dramatically increases your chances of seeing the northern lights from the warm water.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool dating back to 1891 surrounded by geysers and hot springs. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic local experience offers a peaceful soak with stunning rural scenery and occasional northern lights overhead.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore the colorful streets of downtown Reykjavik with a local guide, sampling traditional Icelandic dishes including skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), fermented shark (hákarl), and fresh langoustine. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church, the Harpa Concert Hall, and local art galleries to absorb Iceland's unique Viking-rooted culture.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's stunning rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands and reward yourself with a natural geothermal hot spring soak at the end of the trail. The vivid green, red, and yellow volcanic landscape is unlike anywhere on Earth, and the natural pool is the perfect way to soothe tired muscles under open skies.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in, unwind with a welcome drink and light refreshments prepared by the resort. Settle into your beachfront suite and rest after the journey.

meals.breakfast: On board flight
meals.lunch: On board flight
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome charcuterie board and Icelandic skyr parfait prepared in-room by the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer with the resort concierge before departure. Request a late check-in amenity package. January nights are long and dark — perfect aurora conditions begin immediately.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely gourmet breakfast at the resort's oceanfront restaurant. Take a short walk along the beachfront to breathe in the crisp Arctic air and orient yourself with the surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the world-famous Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa, just minutes from the resort. Enjoy the milky-blue silica-rich geothermal waters, indulge in an in-water massage, and use the premium Retreat Spa facilities. Book the Retreat Spa package for exclusive access to private lagoon areas.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sunset cocktail hour (though January offers very limited daylight, enjoy the dramatic twilight). Dine at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant featuring Icelandic lamb, Arctic char, and locally foraged ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic gourmet breakfast at the resort — smoked salmon, skyr, rye bread, eggs, and fresh pastries
meals.lunch: Lava Restaurant at the Blue Lagoon — Icelandic seafood bisque and open-faced sandwiches overlooking the lagoon
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — pan-seared Arctic char with dill beurre blanc, Icelandic lamb rack, and volcanic salt chocolate lava cake

day_by_day.notes: Book the Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa package well in advance as it sells out quickly. January daylight is only about 5–6 hours, so afternoon visits to the lagoon will be beautifully lit by candlelight ambiance and steam.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided drive along the Reykjanes Peninsula. Explore the dramatic volcanic lava fields, the Bridge Between Continents (spanning the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates), and the Gunnuhver geothermal hot spring area with its boiling mud pools and steam vents.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour — transfer by private car to Reykjavik city center. Explore the colorful streets of downtown with a local expert guide, sampling traditional Icelandic cuisine including hákarl (fermented shark), skyr, kleinur doughnuts, and locally brewed craft beers.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — depart after dinner for a small-group guided jeep excursion into the Icelandic wilderness away from light pollution. Expert guides use real-time aurora forecasts to maximize sighting chances. Hot chocolate and blankets provided.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — Icelandic pancakes with crowberries, smoked trout, and freshly brewed Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Included tastings on the Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour; supplement with a bowl of traditional Icelandic lamb soup at Café Loki
meals.dinner: Dill Restaurant, Reykjavik — Iceland's premier Michelin-starred restaurant; tasting menu featuring hyper-local, seasonal New Nordic cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Aurora activity is weather-dependent. January is one of the best months for northern lights viewing in Iceland. The jeep tour operators will reschedule or offer alternative dates if cloud cover prevents sightings.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer to Reykjavik for a curated visit to the Hallgrímskirkja Church (with panoramic elevator views over the city) and the Harpa Concert Hall. Explore the Sun Voyager sculpture along the waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Iceland for a deep dive into Viking history and Icelandic heritage. Afterward, browse the luxury boutiques and design stores on Laugavegur Street for premium Icelandic wool sweaters, jewelry, and artisan goods.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a private in-suite couples' spa treatment booked through the resort — hot stone massage with geothermal volcanic stones and Icelandic herb body wraps. Early night to prepare for highland adventures ahead.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet with made-to-order eggs and Icelandic smoked meats
meals.lunch: Messinn Restaurant, Reykjavik — renowned for its cast-iron pan-fried fish of the day with butter, capers, and Icelandic herbs
meals.dinner: In-suite private dining experience at the resort — curated 4-course tasting menu delivered by personal butler service

day_by_day.notes: Shopping on Laugavegur Street is ideal for high-end Icelandic brands like 66°North and Geysir. Reserve in-suite spa treatments at least 24 hours in advance through the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to the Golden Circle. Depart early by private luxury vehicle. First stop: Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates meet. Walk the Almannagjá canyon rift in the crisp winter air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Geysir Geothermal Area to witness the famous Strokkur geyser erupting every 5–10 minutes. Lunch at the Geysir Center restaurant. Then drive to the majestic Gullfoss Waterfall — partially frozen in January, creating a spectacular icy spectacle.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort via private car. Relax in the resort's private hot tub or geothermal pool on the beachfront. Optional second Northern Lights Hunt if aurora forecast is favorable — contact tour operator for availability.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast — energy-packed porridge with Icelandic honey, smoked salmon bagel, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Geysir Center Restaurant — lamb stew, fresh bread, and Icelandic dairy products
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant — slow-braised short rib with root vegetable purée, truffle oil, and Icelandic microgreens; paired with Icelandic craft beer flight

day_by_day.notes: Golden Circle roads are generally well-maintained but can be icy in January. Ensure the private driver uses a 4WD vehicle. Dress in thermal layers — temperatures can drop to -10°C near Gullfoss.

day_by_day.morning: Depart for the South Coast adventure. Private luxury 4WD transfer eastward along Route 1. First stop: Seljalandsfoss Waterfall — walk behind the curtain of water (weather permitting in January; ice may restrict access). Continue to Skógafoss Waterfall for dramatic rainbow mist photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach near Vík — marvel at the hexagonal basalt columns, sea stacks, and powerful Atlantic waves. Visit the Reynisdrangar sea stacks. Stop at the iconic red-roofed Kirkjubæjarklaustur church ruins.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a premium overnight accommodation near Vík or return to the resort depending on preference (itinerary assumes day trip return). Enjoy dinner in Vík before private transfer back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — smoked lamb open sandwich, skyr with berries, and Icelandic flatbread
meals.lunch: Skál! Restaurant near Skógafoss — hearty Icelandic fish and chips with homemade tartar sauce and local beer
meals.dinner: Suður-Vík Restaurant, Vík — cozy Icelandic comfort food; lamb soup, grilled fish, and warm apple cake with vanilla cream

day_by_day.notes: Exercise extreme caution at Reynisfjara Beach — sneaker waves are deadly. Never turn your back on the ocean. January conditions can be severe; the driver will assess road safety throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and resort morning. Enjoy a slow breakfast and a private yoga or meditation session arranged by the resort on the beachfront (weather permitting) or in the resort's wellness studio. Take time to journal and absorb the midpoint of the journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak — private transfer to Flúðir village to experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, dating back to 1891. Soak in the naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by geysers and steam vents in a beautifully rustic setting. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep (second attempt/primary booking) — guided small-group jeep tour into the highlands. January darkness from 4 PM provides maximum aurora window. Expert guides track aurora forecasts and drive to optimal viewing locations away from all light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Resort spa breakfast — green smoothie, avocado toast with Icelandic sea salt, poached eggs, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Minibar Bistro near Flúðir — Icelandic tomato soup, freshly baked bread, and local cheeses
meals.dinner: Pre-tour dinner at the resort — seared scallops with cauliflower purée, followed by venison loin with juniper berry jus; pack hot thermos of cocoa for the aurora tour

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is a hidden gem — far more authentic and intimate than commercial spas. Bring a warm robe or rent one on-site. The jeep tour departs around 9 PM for optimal aurora conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter tour over the Reykjanes Peninsula volcanic landscape (book through resort concierge with a local aviation company). Aerial views of lava fields, geothermal vents, and the coastline are truly extraordinary in winter light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Keflavík area's Víkingaheimar (Viking World) Museum — home to a full-size replica Viking ship. Explore the interactive exhibits on Norse seafaring culture. Browse the museum gift shop for premium Icelandic Viking-themed artisan goods.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's bar (brief but vivid January twilight). Private chef's table dinner experience at the resort — watch the head chef prepare a bespoke 6-course tasting menu featuring the finest Icelandic seasonal ingredients, paired with Icelandic and international wines.

meals.breakfast: Resort full breakfast — Icelandic rye bread with smoked salmon, scrambled eggs with chives, fresh pastries, and Icelandic dairy
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Víkingaheimar café — Skyr bowl with granola, smoked fish wrap, and Icelandic sparkling water
meals.dinner: Private chef's table at the resort — 6-course tasting menu: langoustine bisque, cured Arctic char, lamb tartare, skyr sorbet palate cleanser, slow-roasted reindeer, and Icelandic birch-smoked chocolate mousse

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tours are weather-dependent and must be booked at least 3–5 days in advance. The chef's table experience should be reserved upon arrival at the resort. Dress elegantly for the chef's table dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike — depart early by private super-jeep for the stunning Highlands. Trek through Iceland's iconic rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains. The landscape is surreal in winter with snow-dusted multicolored peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the Landmannalaugar geothermal area and soak in the natural hot spring river surrounded by snow and mountains. The contrast of hot geothermal water against the icy winter air is an unforgettable experience. Guided naturalist explains the volcanic geology.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey to the resort by super-jeep. Stop at a remote highland viewpoint for a final aurora scan if skies are clear. Arrive back at the resort for a restorative late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Packed premium resort breakfast box for the road — thermos of coffee, smoked salmon sandwiches, fruit, skyr, and Icelandic chocolate
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the resort chef — lamb wraps, hard-boiled eggs, cheese, crackers, dried fruit, and hot soup in a thermos consumed at Landmannalaugar
meals.dinner: Late dinner at the resort restaurant — warming lamb shank with root vegetables, potato gratin, and red wine reduction; finish with warm Icelandic rice pudding

day_by_day.notes: Landmannalaugar in January requires a highly experienced super-jeep driver with F-road mountain experience. Some highland roads may be closed — the guide will confirm access the day before. Bring extra thermal layers and waterproof gear.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely resort morning. Enjoy a long soak in the resort's private geothermal pool or hot tub overlooking the ocean. Book a 90-minute deep tissue or hot stone massage at the resort spa to recover from the highland hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided snowmobile tour on a glacier — transfer to Langjökull Glacier (approximately 2 hours from the resort) for an exhilarating snowmobile excursion across Europe's second-largest glacier. Optional: glacier ice cave exploration with a certified glaciologist guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a premium whisky or Brennivín (Icelandic schnapps) tasting session at the resort bar. Dine at the resort's fine-dining restaurant with a focus on Icelandic seafood.

meals.breakfast: Resort spa breakfast — bircher muesli, smoked trout on rye, fresh berries, and green tea
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the glacier tour — hot lamb soup in thermos, rye bread sandwiches, chocolate, and energy bars
meals.dinner: Resort seafood tasting menu — oysters with Icelandic mignonette, langoustine with garlic butter, grilled monkfish with saffron sauce, and Arctic char with wild mushroom risotto

day_by_day.notes: Glacier tours require advance booking and are weather-dependent. All safety equipment (helmets, suits, boots) is provided. The ice cave exploration is an additional premium add-on worth every króna.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer back to Reykjavik for a cultural deep dive. Visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) — a remarkable underground museum built around a 10th-century Viking longhouse excavation. Then explore the Árbær Open Air Museum for a living history experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Whales of Iceland Exhibition — the world's largest whale exhibition with life-size whale models. Afterward, enjoy a private art gallery tour in the 101 Reykjavik district, exploring contemporary Icelandic art at Listasafn Íslands (National Gallery of Iceland).
day_by_day.evening: Final Reykjavik evening — cocktails at Skál! Craft Bar on Laugavegur, followed by dinner at Grillið Restaurant atop the Radisson Blu Saga Hotel with panoramic city views. Return to resort by private car.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full Icelandic spread with all favorites plus freshly made waffles with Icelandic butter and jam
meals.lunch: Kopar Restaurant at the Old Harbour, Reykjavik — fresh lobster soup, fish of the day, and Icelandic flatbread
meals.dinner: Grillið Restaurant, Reykjavik — premium tasting menu with panoramic views; Icelandic beef tenderloin, pan-seared halibut, and classic crème brûlée

day_by_day.notes: Grillið is one of Reykjavik's most celebrated fine-dining restaurants — reserve at least a week in advance. The Old Harbour area is particularly atmospheric in winter with fishing boats and seabirds.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided horseback riding tour on Icelandic horses — experience the unique tölt gait of the purebred Icelandic horse through lava fields and coastal paths near the resort. Icelandic horses are exceptionally gentle and suitable for all experience levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Blue Lagoon for a final luxurious soak — this time book the exclusive Retreat Spa private suite experience with personal attendant, in-water float therapy, and a curated spa menu. The perfect way to spend a final full afternoon in Iceland.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the resort — request the resort's premium private dining setup on the beachfront (weather permitting) or in a private dining room. Toast the journey with Icelandic sparkling water and champagne under the stars, hoping for a final aurora display overhead.

meals.breakfast: Celebratory resort breakfast — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, freshly squeezed Arctic berry juice, and Icelandic pastries
meals.lunch: Retreat Spa restaurant at the Blue Lagoon — elevated Icelandic cuisine in the exclusive spa dining room; langoustine salad and mushroom risotto
meals.dinner: Private farewell dinner at the resort — 7-course chef's tasting menu: best of Icelandic cuisine curated over the full 12 days, paired with Icelandic and French wines, ending with a custom dessert platter

day_by_day.notes: Request the resort to set up a private aurora alert system for the farewell evening — staff can wake guests if the aurora appears. Horseback riding tours should be booked 48 hours in advance. Pack bags tonight for early departure tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at the resort. Enjoy one last soak in the geothermal pool at sunrise (or pre-dawn in January). Savor a final leisurely breakfast. Take a slow walk along the beachfront to collect memories and perhaps a few volcanic pebbles as souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the resort. Private luxury transfer to Keflavík International Airport. Depart Iceland with extraordinary memories of northern lights, hot springs, volcanic landscapes, and world-class cuisine.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Settle in with Icelandic chocolates and skyr purchased at the airport's duty-free as delicious souvenirs of this extraordinary 13-day premium Icelandic adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — full spread including all Icelandic favorites; take your time and savor every bite
meals.lunch: Fljótt og Gott or Geysir Bistro at Keflavík Airport — Icelandic lamb soup or fish dish for a final taste of Iceland before departure
meals.dinner: On board departure flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for airport check-in and security. The airport has excellent duty-free shopping for Icelandic spirits (Brennivín), chocolates, skincare (Blue Lagoon products), and woolen goods. Confirm private transfer time with resort concierge the evening before.
